frozen_candidate_root_contribution: SUBSTITUTION: the relation in which one entity comes to stand in the place of another — a counterpart displacing an original, such that where item A was, item B now is. The root supplies only the substitution relation itself (one-for-another, put-in-place-of); it does NOT by itself fix the direction (which item is original vs. replacement), the evaluative polarity (upgrade vs. downgrade), or the domain — those come from construction, participants, and context.

internal_discovery.candidate_root_contribution: SUBSTITUTION: the relation in which one entity comes to stand in the place of another — a counterpart displacing an original, such that where item A was, item B now is. The root supplies only the substitution relation itself (one-for-another, put-in-place-of); it does NOT by itself fix the direction (which item is original vs. replacement), the evaluative polarity (upgrade vs. downgrade), or the domain — those come from construction, participants, and context.
internal_discovery.plain_explanation:
Across every form-family the invariant is "B comes to stand where A was." This is repeatedly made explicit by three overlapping construction markers, but the substitution relation is present even when unmarked:

(1) makāna ("in the place of") — 16:101 "baddalnā āyatan makāna āyatin" (We substitute one sign IN PLACE OF another); 7:95 "baddalnā makāna al-sayyiʾati al-ḥasanata" (We put good IN PLACE OF evil); 4:20 "istibdāla zawjin makāna zawjin" (replacement of one wife IN PLACE OF another). These pin the core meaning precisely: an item installed where another stood.

(2) ghayr ("other than") — 2:59 / 7:162 "baddala ... qawlan ghayra alladhī qīla lahum" (substituted a word OTHER THAN what was said); 4:56 "baddalnāhum julūdan ghayrahā" (replaced them with OTHER skins); 14:48 "tubaddalu al-arḍu ghayra al-arḍ" (the earth is exchanged for OTHER than the earth); 47:38 / 9:39 "yastabdil qawman ghayrakum" (replace you with an OTHER people). The replacer is explicitly the not-original.

(3) bi- / accusative of exchange (A-for-B) — 4:2 "tatabaddalū al-khabītha bil-ṭayyib" (take the bad IN EXCHANGE FOR the good); 2:108 "yatabaddal al-kufra bil-īmān" (takes disbelief for faith); 2:61 "atastabdilūna alladhī huwa adnā bi-alladhī huwa khayr" (exchange the lower FOR the better); 33:52 "an tabaddala bihinna min azwāj" (exchange them for other wives).

Form-family coverage of the same relation:
- V(II) baddala (transitive/causative substitution): "yubaddilu ... sayyiʾātihim ḥasanāt" (25:70, replaces their evil deeds with good), "yubaddilannahum ... khawfihim amnan" (24:55, replaces their fear with security), 34:16 gardens replaced by inferior gardens, 40:26 "yubaddila dīnakum" (change/replace your religion), 48:15 "yubaddilū kalāma Allāh" (alter = substitute-for God's speech), 50:29 "mā yubaddalu al-qawlu ladayya" (the sentence is not swapped out before Me), 56:61/70:41/76:28 "nubaddila ... amthālakum / khayran minhum" (replace you with your likes / better).
- V(IV) abdala (provide-in-exchange): 18:81, 66:5, 68:32 "yubdila(humā/hu/nā) khayran minhu/minhā/minkunna" — God gives a better one IN PLACE OF what was lost.
- V(V) tabaddala (take-for-self in exchange): 2:108, 4:2, 33:52 — subject acquires B while giving up A.
- V(X)/N(X) istabdala / istibdāl (seek/effect substitution): 2:61, 47:38, 9:39, 4:20.
- N(II) tabdīl / mubaddil (act / agent of substitution): the negated "lā tabdīla / lā mubaddila li-kalimāti(hi) / li-khalqi llāh / li-sunnati llāh" (10:64, 18:27, 6:115, 6:34, 30:30, 33:62, 35:43, 48:23) = God's words/creation/way admit NO substitution — nothing can be installed in their place; "mā baddalū tabdīlan" (33:23) = they effected no swap of their commitment.
- ADJ/noun badal (the substitute item): 18:50 "biʾsa lil-ẓālimīna badalan" — Iblis and his offspring are a wretched SUBSTITUTE (taken as protectors in place of God).

In every case, subtracting form and construction leaves the same residue: one thing standing in the place of another.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: Subtractions applied to isolate the residue: (a) FORM — V(II) contributes transitive/causative framing ("cause B to stand for A"), V(IV) the benefactive "provide in exchange," V(V) the reflexive "take in exchange for oneself," V(X) the desiderative/seeking "procure a substitute," N(II) tabdīl the nominalized act (and mubaddil the agent), ADJ/noun badal the substitute-item; none of these add or remove the substitution relation, they only orient its argument structure. (b) CONSTRUCTION — makāna supplies the explicit "in-place-of" slot, ghayr marks the replacer as non-original, bi- and the second accusative supply the exchanged-for counterpart, and negation (lā ... tabdīla) supplies "no substitution is possible." Direction (which is original) and polarity (better/worse: khayran minhu vs. adnā, ḥasanāt vs. sayyiʾāt) are ENTIRELY construction/context, NOT root. (c) PARTICIPANTS — God, wrongdoers, Pharaoh, the wronged; irrelevant to residue. (d) CONTEXT — legal (bequest 2:181, wives 4:20/33:52, orphans' property 4:2), eschatological (14:48 earth changed, 4:56 skins renewed), narrative (2:59 word altered), theological (immutability of kalimāt/sunna/khalq). After all four subtractions the constant is the bare substitution relation: B-in-place-of-A.
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: The hardest cases are those where no second (replacer) item is surfaced and the sense looks like bare "change/alteration" rather than "A-for-B substitution": 33:23 "wa-mā baddalū tabdīlan" (they did not change [their commitment] in the least) and the immutability formulas 30:30 "lā tabdīla li-khalqi llāh," 50:29 "mā yubaddalu al-qawlu ladayya," 33:62/35:43/48:23 "lā tajidu li-sunnati llāhi tabdīlan." Here only ONE item (the covenant, creation, the decree, the sunna) is named. Reconciliation: these are all NEGATED or steadfastness contexts, and negated substitution still presupposes the substitution relation — "no tabdīl" means precisely "nothing installed in its place," "no counterpart admitted," which is why 35:43 can immediately contrast it with taḥwīl (diverting-away): the two negations deny two distinct operations. The counterpart (the would-be replacer) is implicit but structurally required — you cannot "swap out X" without an incoming Y, even if Y is left unspecified. So these reduce to "the relation whereby a counterpart takes X's place — here asserted impossible," not to a rootless notion of qualitative modification. The residue holds.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: Strongest alternative: the core is "CHANGE / ALTERATION" (qualitative modification of an item's state) rather than the sharper "SUBSTITUTION (one item put in the place of another)." This hypothesis also covers the data loosely, because every substitution entails a change. Internal arbitration decisively favors substitution: (1) the recurrent explicit "makāna" ('in the place of': 16:101, 7:95, 4:20) encodes a positional swap, not mere alteration; (2) the recurrent "ghayr" ('other than': 2:59, 7:162, 4:56, 14:48, 47:38, 9:39) names a distinct second entity that comes in — alteration of a single persisting item would not require an "other"; (3) the exchange constructions with bi- (4:2, 2:108, 2:61, 33:52) present two items trading places; (4) V(IV) abdala "give in exchange a better one" (66:5, 68:32, 18:81) and the badal noun (18:50, a substitute protector) are about a replacement entity, not a modified state. The "change" reading is a bleached over-generalization; wherever the data adds specificity, it specifies substitution. The pure-change hypothesis cannot explain why "other/in-place-of/in-exchange-for" saturate the corpus.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: Nearest semantic neighbors and the boundary: (1) ḥ-w-l (taḥwīl) — decisively separated INTERNALLY at 35:43, where "lā tajidu ... tabdīlan wa-lā tajidu ... taḥwīlan" pairs and CONTRASTS them: bdl = substituting a counterpart in the thing's place; ḥwl = turning/diverting/removing the thing itself elsewhere. The two negations would be redundant if bdl meant mere change. (2) gh-y-r (ghayr, taghyīr) — 'otherness/being-different'; bdl repeatedly USES ghayr as a construction argument (the replacer is 'other'), showing bdl is the operation that installs the other, not the state of difference itself. (3) ṣ-r-f (turning-away/diverting) and q-l-b (overturning) — reorientation of one item, no incoming counterpart. (4) n-q-l — transfer/relocation of an item without a replacer filling its slot. bdl uniquely requires a filled-slot swap: an original vacated and a counterpart installed. Falsifiability condition: the substitution core would be REFUTED if some occurrence used a bdl-form for a purely qualitative modification of a single item that keeps its identity and place with NO counterpart entering even implicitly (e.g., 'the water became warmer'), or for mere removal with an empty slot left behind. No such occurrence exists in the 44.
internal_discovery.rationale: A single non-empty contribution — SUBSTITUTION, the installation of a counterpart in the place of an original — is recoverable at the surface in all 44 occurrences and needs no forcing. It is positively marked by makāna ('in place of'), ghayr ('other than'), and bi-/second-accusative exchange constructions across the majority of tokens, and it is presupposed even in the negated immutability formulas (lā tabdīla li-kalimāt/khalq/sunna) and the unspecified-counterpart cases (33:23), which deny the very relation the root names. The core is sharply distinct from its nearest neighbor ḥ-w-l, and the distinction is confirmed INTERNALLY by 35:43's contrastive pairing of tabdīl with taḥwīl — the strongest possible in-corpus evidence that bdl is not generic 'change' but specifically 'replacement-by-counterpart.' The competing 'mere change/alteration' hypothesis is a bleached superset that the makāna/ghayr/bi- evidence rules out wherever the text adds detail. Direction and evaluative polarity are supplied by construction rather than the root, but the substitution RELATION is determinate and surface-recoverable everywhere, warranting STRONG. No occurrence is left unreconciled; inconsistent_refs is empty.

adversarial_verification.notes: Adversarial sweep of all 44 occurrences found NO genuine failing occurrence. The frozen candidate (SUBSTITUTION: B comes to stand where A was; direction/polarity/domain left to context) survives every cluster: explicit makāna markers (16:101, 7:95, 4:20), explicit ghayr markers (2:59, 7:162, 4:56, 14:48, 47:38, 9:39, 10:15), A-for-B exchange (2:108, 4:2, 2:61, 33:52, 14:28, 27:11), V(IV) compensation-substitution (18:81, 66:5, 68:32), V(II) replace-with (24:55, 25:70, 34:16, 56:61, 70:41, 76:28), and the negated tabdīl/mubaddil group (10:64, 18:27, 6:115, 6:34, 30:30, 33:62, 35:43, 48:23, 33:23) where the substitution relation is exactly what is denied. ADJ badal (18:50) = the substitute-item taken "min dūnī" (instead of God), contextually supported not circular. Hardest cases were the seemingly generic-"alter" tokens 40:26 (yubaddila dīnakum) and 48:15 (yubaddilū kalāma Allāh): these resolve cleanly because altering God's word is modeled in-corpus as substituting other-than-what-was-said (2:59 qawlan ghayra alladhī qīla), i.e. installing different content in place of the original — the two-item relation holds without strain. Distinctiveness is decisively confirmed by 35:43, which juxtaposes bdl (tabdīlan) with ḥwl (taḥwīlan), demonstrating bdl (discrete counterpart installed where A stood) is distinct from ḥwl (transfer/divert-elsewhere) and from ghyr/ṣrf/qlb (internal alteration/turning). The root is not an elastic blob: it requires a two-item one-for-another relation, discriminating against mere becoming-different. Falsifiable — a failure would be a token meaning quantitative increase or "begin" (the distinct root bdʾ, b-d-ʾ); none occurs. Verdict SUPPORTED.
